subject: Re: MAP & Benchmarking logistics — access, windows, and close timeline
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@zephyrsys.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Narang <priya.narang@zephyrsys.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Performance MAP & test access

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost profile looked promising. We need to lock down a mutual action plan (MAP) to validate performance under our load and hit a close by EOM. High level asks from our side:

- A short MAP that lists the benchmarking plan (TTFT, p50/p95 latency, sustained throughput, and concurrency targets).
- Access to an isolated test environment and temporary API keys for synthetic load (we can run both synthetic and a small replay of production traces).
- Preferred load windows (we're PST and can do weekday nights).

Can someone from your side propose specific windows and required artifacts? Also please include a suggested runbook so our SRE can pair during the runs.

Goal: complete full perf validation and capture results by Nov 15 so procurement can finalize the contract.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior SRE, Zephyr Systems

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@zephyrsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & test access

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (solutions lead) and Karthik (perf lead) to scope the MAP.

Short answer: we can deliver an actionable MAP and a runbook with dedicated test keys. Proposed next steps below; I'll attach a draft MAP and a proposed schedule.

Immediate asks for you:
- Confirm whether you want replay of production traces or only synthetic. Replay will need sanitized traces and an address-of-record for the test endpoint.
- Confirm max concurrent sessions you want validated (you mentioned 300 concurrent requests at demo).

We're free to run the main load windows on Nov 13 (night) and Nov 14 (night) PST. If those work we'll target a final results summary by end of day Nov 15.

Attaching: Zephyr_MAP_v1.xlsx (draft MAP), load_window_schedule.ics (proposed slots).

Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0113

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@zephyrsys.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & test access

Thanks — I reviewed Neha's draft. Quick notes from the perf side:

- Test objectives: TTFT under cold start and warm-cache conditions, sustained throughput at target concurrency, token-level p50/p95 latencies, and service degradation behavior under overload.
- Workload: we recommend a mix: 70% synthetic steady-state (fixed prompt lengths for baseline) + 30% trace-replay for tail behavior. Bring a 1-hour sample trace for the replay (sanitized).
- Targets to validate: 200–300 concurrent requests, TTFT < 2200ms for cold start, p95 token latency < 80ms for warm cached runs, sustained throughput >= 350 tokens/sec per GPU cluster (we'll map to your requested keys).

Logistics: I will create temp API keys scoped to a dedicated test project (data isolated), provide an endpoint in our staging region (us-west-2), and share a short runbook. For pairing, Karthik and I will join the run windows and watch the traces and metrics.

Can you confirm:
- Which prompt sizes and model variant you want us to use (we have quantized v1/standard v2 ops).
- Whether you need encrypted logs exported to your S3 (we can enable if required — note this adds 24–48 hrs to setup).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@zephyrsys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & test access

Thanks Marissa — that plan looks good. Answers below:

- We'll do 2 prompt profiles: short (avg 30 tokens) and long (avg 180 tokens). Use the standard v2 model variant.
- We'll provide a 1-hour sanitized trace (short prompts only) for a single replay run.
- Encrypted logs to our S3 would be ideal — we can get you an IAM role; confirm what format you need.
- Confirming we prefer Nov 13 11pm–2am PST and Nov 14 11pm–2am PST for the main windows. If you could provision keys and endpoint today, we can validate connectivity tonight.

One ask on the MAP: please include a final acceptance criteria checklist (what counts as pass/fail for each metric) so procurement has a clear gating for close.

Jordan
Senior SRE, Zephyr Systems

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@zephyrsys.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & test access

Jordan — thanks for the quick confirmations. Closing loop:

What we did (summary) — internal + external run windows completed Nov 13/14 as planned with Marissa & Karthik pairing. Attached is a concise results CSV (bench_results_summary.csv) and an updated MAP workbook (Zephyr_MAP_v1.xlsx) with acceptance criteria included. Highlights:

- Cold TTFT (cold VM + cold KV cache): median 2.05s, 95th 2.48s (target < 2.2s pass marginal; noted one outlier at 2.9s tied to load spike).
- Warm cached token p95 latency: 74ms (target < 80ms) — pass.
- Sustained throughput: 370 tokens/sec sustained across the cluster during the 30-minute steady-state window (target >= 350) — pass.
- Concurrency: validated up to 320 concurrent sessions with graceful degradation (queueing and 429 at 340+). Recommended operational cap: 320 concurrency per project with autoscaling cushion.

Acceptance checklist (from MAP):
- Short prompt p95 < 80ms (PASS)
- Long prompt sustained throughput >= 350 tokens/sec (PASS)
- TTFT cold < 2.2s (MARGINAL) — see comment and follow-up item below
- No data leakage; logs delivered to your S3 (ENABLED)

Follow ups:
- Karthik will investigate the single cold-outlier (likely transient GPU warmup/slot scheduling). We can re-run a short cold-only window if you want tighter guarantees.
- I'll attach the HubSpot deal link in the MAP and add a procurement gating row. We propose final paperwork sign-off by Nov 20 to meet your internal EOM target.

Attachments: bench_results_summary.csv (summary metrics + per-run traces), Zephyr_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated MAP with acceptance criteria), load_window_schedule.ics

Next steps / asks from Zephyr:
- Confirm acceptance of marginal TTFT and whether you want a re-run for cold-start tightening.
- Share IAM role for S3 logs if you want continued exports beyond the test window.

If you confirm acceptance, I'll mark the MAP milestone as complete and route the paperwork to procurement for the final commits.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
